prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Name & Officialize Your New Pet Companion"]
1: ["Sign In to Protect Your Saved Pet", "Your companion and customizations are linked to your account. Signing in guarantees your pet data will never reset or vanish."]
2: ["Initializing desktop graphics engine and rendering your pet companion..."]
3: ["Choose Your Pet Creation Path"]
4: ["Configure Trait Settings", "Configure Pet Personality & Voice", "Select your desktop companion's interaction preferences and voice responses before completing setup.", "Behavioral Traits"]
5: ["Your Companion is Ready on Your Desktop!", "Click and drag to move your pet around your screen. Right-click the tray icon anytime to access controls, chat, or hide your companion."]
6: ["Signing in anchors your pet to your account so progress is preserved across app updates and re-installations."]
7: ["Enable desktop notification to get alerted as soon as your pet is live on screen."]
8: []
9: ["Welcome to Your Desktop Companion!"]
